response.consequence: Anyone can make the endpoint return a 500 with a negative limit or offset. Anyone can also force the server to load and serialize an entire large group in one request, which defeats the pagination this change adds.
response.explanation: GroupsController#members, which any user who can see the group can call, converts params[:limit] and params[:offset] with to_i and passes them straight to limit() and offset(). Nothing clamps them. A negative limit, such as limit=-1, produces an invalid SQL LIMIT on PostgreSQL, so the request fails with a 500. A very large limit, such as limit=1000000, loads and serializes every member of the group in one request. The old code applied limit/offset only to automatic groups. This change makes every group go through this path, and the new meta block echoes the raw values back to the client.

response.consequence: For groups whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size, the admin UI offers a next page that is always empty. The last real page is never marked as last.
response.explanation: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), it returns 2 instead of 1. currentPage is 1 at offset 0, so showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) is false. The "next" action then sets offset to min(0+50, 50) = 50 and calls findMembers, which loads an empty page. The same off-by-one affects every exact-multiple count (100, 150, and so on).
